method.title: How I work
method.quote: I test software the way I was taught to do maths: state the problem precisely, argue every step, don't skip details.

steps.title: State the problem precisely
steps.text: Before I test or optimize anything, I write down what is given, the rules and the goal. That's how a slow CI pipeline became an optimization model.

link.label: See it in the CI case →

steps.title: Test at the layer where the defect can exist
steps.text: Rules and contracts get API tests; user flows get end-to-end tests. Running the same specs against a mock and the real API found a defect neither run could see alone.

steps.title: Use explicit test-design techniques
steps.text: Equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables and state transitions, named in each test, so a reviewer can see what is covered and what isn't.

principle.label: Principle
principle.title: When there is no perfect oracle, test relationships and invariants.
principle.text: Quantitative and AI-driven systems don't always have one exact expected value. Then I test what must stay true: constraints, consistency between related inputs, metamorphic relationships, numerical tolerances and regressions against known outputs. It's how I test the core of CI Shard Advisor, and the whole point of my Solver Validation Lab.

jobs.context: Telecom OSS platform for EWE, a German telecom and energy provider, built on TM Forum standards
bullets: Design and run the tests for TM Forum service-order flows in Jira and Xray: add, modify, delete, suspend and reactivate.
Building API automation with Karate against TM Forum APIs.
Built a one-click Postman smoke suite that checks every service after a production deployment.

jobs.context: International cybersecurity SaaS for threat modeling, remote
bullets: Built a Python MILP model to split end-to-end tests across CI containers: 42% faster in a one-worker benchmark. Modelling the 5 production workers showed 4 containers instead of 7 would be about 8% faster and 41% cheaper.
Led the testing strategy for the Security Content module, a core part of the product, across backend, API and frontend.
Designed Playwright and TypeScript automation for a combinatorial rules engine, with Page Objects, API-backed setup and data factories.
Automated backend APIs in Java with REST Assured and JUnit 5: schema validation, negative cases and traceability.
Worked on the TestCafe to Playwright migration: about 80% less run time and a more stable suite.
